# The provenance file on Tajikarao

*The provenance file for Tajikarao. Nothing here is unsourced; that is what the file is for.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **手力男神** — "Strong hand man". On record: Kojiki, Ama-no-Iwato narrative (Kamitsumaki), Nihon Shoki, Age of the Gods, Scroll I, Philippi, Kojiki (Princeton, 1968), Aston, Nihongi (1896).

**2. The narrative record.** **The Sun Withdraws into the Rock** — The crisis begins with Susanoo's rampage.  The storm god, granted leave from heaven, trampled down the ridges of Amaterasu's rice-paddies, filled in her irrigation ditches, and finally flayed the heavenly piebald colt and hurled its carcass through the roof of the sacred weaving-hall, so that a weaving-maiden, struck by the flying shuttle, died at her loom (Kojiki). **The Laughter at the Cave Door** — The assembled kami answered with misdirection.  The goddess Ame-no-Uzume bound up her sleeves with a heavenly vine, took a bundle of sasaki grass for a headdress, overturned a tub before the cave, and stamped out a lewd, rattling dance upon it, baring herself to the roaring laughter of the whole assembly.

**3. The physical record.** No excavated site attests Tajikarao himself from the Kofun period or earlier; his evidence is cultic and textual. The clearest material anchor is Amanoiwato-jinja above the Takachiho Gorge in Miyazaki Prefecture, where the cave of the myth is identified and a worship-hall faces the cliff across the gorge. His principal shrine, the Middle Shrine (Chū-sha) of Togakushi in Nagano, stands within a complex whose documented history runs from the mid-ninth century, when the Tendai temple Togakushi-san was founded on the mountain; the present shrine buildings are early modern, and the famous cryptomeria avenue to the Oku-sha was planted in the medieval period. Kagura masks and votive tablets depicting the cave scene, from the early modern period onward, are held in shrine collections across western Japan.

**4. The current holding.** The temple at [/tajikarao/](/tajikarao/), classified Tier 2. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

**5. The documented resonances.** **Construction & Engineering**, **Sports, Fitness & Competition**, **Defense, Military & Security** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/tajikarao/blog/resonance/).

**6. The primary sources.** [Kojiki](/texts/kojiki/), [Nihon Shoki](/texts/nihon-shoki/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**7. The continuing record.** Tajikarao's living monument is Togakushi.  The shrine complex above Nagano, approached by an avenue of centuries-old cedars, draws pilgrims and hikers to the Oku-sha and worshippers seeking strength and favorable outcomes to its Middle Shrine; the mountains acquired a second, separate fame in the medieval period as the legendary home of the Togakure-ryū ninja tradition — the 'hidden door' serving concealment as well as revelation.
